documents.title: Generative AI Use in Education
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines from the Office of the Provost on generative AI in teaching and learning, with guiding principles, guidelines for instructors, guidelines for students, and recommendations for implementation. Instructors decide whether, when and how students may use GenAI, and students must assume AI is not allowed unless the instructor says so. The document also covers disclosure, privacy, bias, human grading oversight, detector limits, and AI literacy.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule for all courses: it says instructors "may determine whether, when, and how GenAI should be integrated" and must state per assignment "when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI". Its only default is a fallback for silent syllabi ("assume it isn't"), so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: A preamble stating purpose and scope: it "establishes guiding principles for the responsible use of GenAI in teaching and learning". P56 (institution-wide framework) fits because it sets the university-level principles.
units.anchor: establishes guiding principles for the responsible use of GenAI in teaching and learning

units.why: Defines GenAI as "systems capable of generating new content", which sets what the guidelines cover. P61 is the definitions type.
units.anchor: we consider GenAI to be systems capable of generating new content

units.why: Gives a rationale: prepare students "to use AI effectively, safely, and ethically" for "professional purposes". That is the learn-AI-as-professional-skill argument (P44).
units.anchor: the need to prepare students to use AI effectively, safely, and ethically

units.why: Lists "potential GenAI uses for instructors" (designing a course, developing lectures, feedback). It names what instructors may use AI for in their teaching work, so P59; it is descriptive rather than a directive.
units.anchor: Potential GenAI uses for instructors include designing a course, developing lectures
units.fit_note: Descriptive list of potential uses, not a directive; also mentions data analysis (P89) and accessibility (P97).

units.why: Names "potential uses for students": a "personal tutor", summarizing, generating ideas, drafting, self-testing. The first-named use is tutoring for understanding, so P12; the others (P14, P15, P91) share the sentence.
units.anchor: Potential uses for students include using GenAI as a personal tutor
units.fit_note: Also lists summarizing, idea generation, drafting and self-testing (P14, P15, P91); stated as potential uses, not rules.

units.why: Lists challenges including "harmful or biased content" and "marginalizing diverse voices". This names bias and harms (P53).
units.anchor: the potential for generating harmful or biased content
units.fit_note: Sentence also lists fabricated information, privacy, IP and replacement of work.

units.why: Names that GenAI can "replace work" rather than enhance it, a risk that it displaces the work learning depends on. P121 is nearest; the sentence does not mention human contact, so this is a partial fit.
units.anchor: GenAI’s potential to not only enhance but also replace work
units.fit_note: Says AI may replace work; does not mention displacing human interaction or feedback.

units.why: States the values behind the guidelines ("core Meliora values", "human-centered approach"). P56 is the framework and principles type.
units.anchor: We promote a human-centered approach to GenAI implementation

units.why: Says "different disciplines and educational contexts may require varied approaches", acknowledging variation below the university rule. P85 (units set own rules) is nearest; P04 is instructor-level and this speaks of disciplines.
units.anchor: different disciplines and educational contexts may require varied approaches
units.fit_note: Acknowledgement of variation, not an explicit grant of authority to schools or departments.

units.why: A recommendation that the university "invest in necessary resources". It is an institutional capacity commitment, not a use rule: P122.
units.anchor: invest in necessary resources to balance innovation with responsible implementation
units.fit_note: Also mentions agile tool evaluation (P65) and promoting literacy (P70).

units.why: States the guidelines will change: "regular review and updates". P54 revisit the policy regularly.
units.anchor: the need for regular review and updates to ensure our guidelines remain relevant

units.why: Principle "Student Learning": all "should prioritize learning and engagement over excessive reliance on GenAI". The reason is that reliance displaces learning, so P41; it cautions rather than bans.
units.anchor: prioritize learning and engagement over excessive reliance on GenAI
units.fit_note: Cautions against excessive reliance, not a limit on a named use.

units.why: Principle "Academic Freedom": instructors "may determine whether, when, and how GenAI should be integrated". The decision is left to instructors, so P04, and no university default is set.
units.anchor: may determine whether, when, and how GenAI should be integrated into their teaching activities

units.why: Principle "Accountability": all members "are responsible for the accuracy of all GenAI-assisted work". Ownership of what is produced: P29 rather than P31 because the focus is responsibility for the work.
units.anchor: responsible for the accuracy of all GenAI-assisted work
units.fit_note: Frames responsibility as accuracy of the work.

units.why: "Users should review, question and evaluate all GenAI output" is a verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: Users should review, question and evaluate all GenAI output

units.why: Principle "Academic Integrity": GenAI use must not "compromise honesty or fairness". The reason given is honesty and fairness, so P95 rather than P36, since no misconduct classification is made here.
units.anchor: GenAI use does not compromise honesty or fairness

units.why: AI use falls under an existing policy: "follow the University of Rochester academic honesty policy for their school". P77 comply with existing university policy.
units.anchor: follow the University of Rochester academic honesty policy for their school

units.why: Principle "Bias": tools are "trained on large, unmoderated datasets" and users should "avoid incorporating biases and inaccuracies". Names bias harm: P53.
units.anchor: avoid incorporating biases and inaccuracies into their work
units.fit_note: Also a duty to check output for inaccuracies (P31).

units.why: Principle "Privacy and Security" asks users to "adhere to university principles of respect for intellectual property". P52 covers IP.
units.anchor: adhere to university principles of respect for intellectual property
units.fit_note: General respect for IP, not ownership of AI inputs and outputs.

units.why: "Should not upload to public GenAI platforms confidential and/or proprietary information" protects data. P50 rather than P49 because it concerns confidential university data, not course materials.
units.anchor: should not upload to public GenAI platforms confidential and/or proprietary information

units.why: Bars sharing "personal or sensitive data, including student information" with public tools: P50.
units.anchor: should not share personal or sensitive data, including student information

units.why: Principle "Transparency": all "should disclose when their work has been created, whole or in part, with a GenAI tool". Disclosure with the work: P24.
units.anchor: disclose when their work has been created, whole or in part, with a GenAI tool

units.why: Disclosures must say "how GenAI was used" and reflect on biases. The reflection element is nearest P26; P25 asks for tool and prompt details that are not named.
units.anchor: Disclosures should specify how GenAI was used
units.fit_note: Asks for how-used detail and reflection on bias, not a full transcript.

units.why: Principle "Equitable Access": the university "should ensure equitable access to GenAI tools". P51 equity and access.
units.anchor: the university should ensure equitable access to GenAI tools and resources

units.why: Instructors "should use course learning outcomes to determine when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI", tying AI decisions to objectives: P83. The must/may/cannot wording resembles P05 but no named tiers are defined.
units.anchor: use course learning outcomes to determine when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI

units.why: Applies the learning-outcomes test to instructors' own AI use: "evaluate their own use of GenAI in their teaching". P83 since the standard is outcomes alignment.
units.anchor: evaluate their own use of GenAI in their teaching

units.why: Instructors "should avoid use of GenAI ... when it might undermine learning outcomes or misrepresent students' abilities". AI is limited when it displaces learning: P41.
units.anchor: avoid use of GenAI, whether by instructor or students, when it might undermine learning outcomes
units.fit_note: Also concerns misrepresenting students' abilities and covers instructor use.

units.why: Limits instructors' own AI use: "refrain from delegating core course responsibilities to GenAI". About what instructors may use AI for in their teaching work: P59, not P46 which is grades only.
units.anchor: refrain from delegating core course responsibilities to GenAI

units.why: Says instructors' AI tools "should complement their work and decision-making", a condition on instructor use of AI in teaching: P59.
units.anchor: these tools should complement their work and decision-making

units.why: Instructors using AI for teaching materials "should disclose and document their GenAI use". AI-made materials disclosed: P48; P47 is about grading and feedback.
units.anchor: they should disclose and document their GenAI use
units.fit_note: Also says disclosure models professionalism and honesty (P112).

units.why: Instructors "should thoroughly review all materials for accuracy and bias" before use. Review of AI-made materials: P48.
units.anchor: thoroughly review all materials for accuracy and bias and revise as necessary

units.why: Course AI policy and handling of violations must "align with the ... academic honesty policy". Compliance with existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: align with the University of Rochester academic honesty policy for their school

units.why: Instructors "are encouraged to discuss with students" honesty values and GenAI issues, going beyond listing a rule: P66.
units.anchor: encouraged to discuss with students both broad academic honesty values and issues

units.why: Instructors "should create and communicate student GenAI course policies", a duty to state expectations: P09.
units.anchor: create and communicate student GenAI course policies

units.why: Policy must say per assignment "when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI", so the rule is set per assignment: P04. The duty to state it is P09, but the assignment-level setting is the point of this passage.
units.anchor: the policy should state when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI
units.fit_note: Also requires stating how to verify, disclose, document and attribute use (P24).

units.why: Policies should be communicated "in writing and discuss[ed] ... with students". Discussion beyond listing the rule: P66.
units.anchor: communicate their GenAI policies in writing and discuss them with students
units.fit_note: Also requires writing the policy (P09).

units.why: Where AI is required, instructors "should ensure equitable access to GenAI for all students": P51.
units.anchor: instructors should ensure equitable access to GenAI for all students

units.why: Instructors "should select GenAI tools that are vetted and supported by the university". Use university-approved tools: P92 (institution-wide rather than P17, a single course tool).
units.anchor: should select GenAI tools that are vetted and supported by the university

units.why: An objecting student gets "an alternative ... that would meet the same learning outcomes". Alternatives so use is not forced: P51.
units.anchor: should provide an alternative for the student that would meet the same learning outcomes
units.fit_note: Alternative is tied to privacy or data-protection objections, and covers required use (P79).

units.why: Instructors "must inform the students that the tool may not always provide accurate information", warning that output may be wrong: P31.
units.anchor: they must inform the students that the tool may not always provide accurate information

units.why: Instructors "should educate students on the tool's strengths, limitations, and proper use" with written guidelines and discussion. Explaining the rules beyond listing them: P66.
units.anchor: Instructors should educate students on the tool’s strengths, limitations, and proper use
units.fit_note: Also asks for verification instructions (P31) and tool education (P70).

units.why: A safe harbor: students "will not be held responsible for errors generated by the tool" when they follow instructions and verify. It reverses P29 (students own all they submit) for required tools, and no type covers it.
units.anchor: Students will not be held responsible for errors generated by the tool
units.uncovered_note: Students are not held responsible for errors from an instructor-required AI tool when they used it as directed and verified output as instructed.

units.why: Says students "are by definition learners" for whom verifying AI output is harder than for experts. Novices cannot judge AI output: P42.
units.anchor: verifying the accuracy of AI outputs is more challenging and time-consuming

units.why: Instructors "should select or develop GenAI tools that preserve usage data". Keeping usage logs is nearest P26 (logs and transcripts), though here the instructor chooses tools that keep logs; no purpose is stated.
units.anchor: select or develop GenAI tools that preserve usage data
units.fit_note: A tool-selection rule for instructors, not a requirement that students submit logs.

units.why: Instructors "retain responsibility for monitoring the tool's outputs and accuracy". Output accuracy oversight: P31.
units.anchor: retain responsibility for monitoring the tool’s outputs and accuracy
units.fit_note: Duty falls on the instructor, not the student.

units.why: Instructors "should provide GenAI literacy instruction to students and course staff": AI-literacy instruction for students and staff, P70.
units.anchor: should provide GenAI literacy instruction to students and course staff

units.why: Instruction should include "modeling responsible, discipline-specific use". Instructors model responsible use: P112.
units.anchor: modeling responsible, discipline-specific use and discussing the strengths and limitations of GenAI
units.fit_note: Also covers discussing inaccuracies, bias and ethics.

units.why: Both groups "should take steps to avoid incorporating these biases". Names bias in output: P53.
units.anchor: should take steps to avoid incorporating these biases into their work

units.why: Non-public information "should never be uploaded into public AI tools" unless the vendor has an approved agreement. Data protection and vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: should never be uploaded into public AI tools—whether free or paid

units.why: Instructors "should only input student data, assignments, or work into university-approved GenAI tools". Use of approved tools: P92 (P50 also fits for privacy; I chose P92 because the rule is to use approved tools).
units.anchor: instructors should only input student data, assignments, or work into university-approved GenAI tools
units.fit_note: Limited to medium and high-risk data and to student work as input.

units.why: States that tools "can infringe on instructor and student intellectual property rights": an IP concern, P52.
units.anchor: GenAI tools can infringe on instructor and student intellectual property rights

units.why: Grading and feedback "require human oversight". Human-in-charge grading: P46.
units.anchor: Grading and feedback are core teaching responsibilities that require human oversight
units.fit_note: Requires human oversight of grading and feedback, not a flat ban on AI grading.

units.why: If using AI in grading, instructors "should pay particular attention to GenAI inaccuracies and biases". Conditions on AI-assisted grading: P101.
units.anchor: instructors should pay particular attention to GenAI inaccuracies and biases

units.why: Instructors "should create and communicate in writing the GenAI work policies that course staff are required to follow". Writing down expectations: P09, though addressed to staff policy.
units.anchor: communicate in writing the GenAI work policies that course staff are required to follow
units.fit_note: Concerns policies for course staff, not student syllabus statements.

units.why: Instructors "should provide access to and training on the GenAI tool" for staff. Training for staff: P70.
units.anchor: the instructor should provide access to and training on the GenAI tool
units.fit_note: Also covers access and legal intersections (P77).

units.why: States detectors "are unreliable, biased, easily defeated, and unable to provide definitive evidence": P39 (do not rely on detectors).
units.anchor: GenAI detection tools are unreliable, biased, easily defeated

units.why: Instructors using detectors "should disclose to students when and how the software will be used". Saying how misuse will be detected: P123.
units.anchor: they should disclose to students when and how the software will be used

units.why: Detection output must not be "the sole basis" for a violation. Detector output as supporting evidence only: P69. The advice to converse with the student is also P57, but the evidence standard is the lead.
units.anchor: avoid using GenAI detection software as the sole basis for an academic honesty policy violation
units.fit_note: Also says to talk with the student and investigate further (P57).

units.why: "Students should use GenAI to enhance—not replace—their learning." AI must not replace the student's thinking: P32.
units.anchor: use GenAI to enhance—not replace—their learning

units.why: The "workout partner" analogy warns that if AI does "the heavy lifting" students "miss out on personal and academic growth". Outsourcing practice undermines skill: P41.
units.anchor: if they let GenAI do the heavy lifting, they miss out on personal

units.why: Students "should aim to understand GenAI course policies". Learn each course's rules: P78.
units.anchor: They should aim to understand GenAI course policies
units.fit_note: Also says AI should not take over the study process (P32).

units.why: "Students should always double-check GenAI-generated information for accuracy": a verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: should always double-check GenAI-generated information for accuracy before using it

units.why: Gives a study-guide example: "cross-reference its answers with their course materials or ask a teaching assistant or instructor". Verification, with human help as one route. P31 fits the check; I chose P72 because the distinctive point is pointing to staff, but this is partial.
units.anchor: cross-reference its answers with their course materials or ask a teaching assistant or instructor
units.fit_note: Mainly a verification instruction (P31); also implies AI-made study guides are acceptable (P14).

units.why: Advises "experimenting with prompts and learning practical ways to interact with GenAI". Prompting advice: P93.
units.anchor: experimenting with prompts and learning practical ways to interact with GenAI will improve results

units.why: States that public platforms "collect data to improve their models", the privacy fact behind the upload rule: P50.
units.anchor: Many public GenAI platforms (like ChatGPT and Claude) collect data to improve their models

units.why: Students "should not share others' personal information, course materials, or any proprietary content" without permission. Course materials into AI: P49.
units.anchor: students should not share others’ personal information, course materials, or any proprietary content
units.fit_note: Allows sharing with clear permission from instructor or creator; also covers personal information (P50).

units.why: Students "should have the autonomy to decide" whether to put their own information or work into public tools. A choice about personal data: P50.
units.anchor: Students should have the autonomy to decide whether to submit their own personal information
units.fit_note: Grants a choice rather than a protective rule.

units.why: "If an instructor has not explicitly stated that GenAI is allowed ... assume it isn't." Fallback rule when a syllabus is silent: P06.
units.anchor: has not explicitly stated that GenAI is allowed for an assignment, assume it isn’t

units.why: "It is up to students to understand and follow the specific policies for each one." Students learn each course's rules: P78; P11 also fits (AI use varies by course) but the duty is on students.
units.anchor: it is up to students to understand and follow the specific policies for each one
units.fit_note: Also says use varies by course (P11).

units.why: "When in doubt, ask the instructor for guidance": P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask the instructor for guidance

units.why: "Unauthorized GenAI use may be considered academic misconduct, similar to plagiarism." Misuse classed as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized GenAI use may be considered academic misconduct

units.why: Instructors "may require ... acknowledging their use or providing transcripts of their AI interactions". Transcripts are the most specific element: P26; acknowledgment is P24.
units.anchor: instructors may require transparency, such as students acknowledging their use or providing transcripts
units.fit_note: Also covers acknowledgment of use (P24); instructor-optional.

units.why: Student TAs "should talk to the instructor about expectations for using GenAI" in grading, feedback or instruction. Ask first: P10.
units.anchor: they should talk to the instructor about expectations for using GenAI
units.fit_note: Addressed to student TAs and peer educators about their staff duties.

units.why: "Unless the instructor says otherwise, assume that using GenAI in these roles is not permitted." Silence means no, for peer educators: P06.
units.anchor: Unless the instructor says otherwise, assume that using GenAI in these roles is not permitted

units.why: "All GenAI use must align with the applicable academic integrity standards": existing policy applies, P77.
units.anchor: All GenAI use must align with the applicable academic integrity standards

units.why: Plagiarism: "Don't present GenAI-generated work as your own without proper attribution". Attribution required, so P24 rather than P19 (AI work is allowed if attributed).
units.anchor: Don’t present GenAI-generated work as your own without proper attribution

units.why: Cheating: "Don't use GenAI to complete assignments unless you have explicit permission." Students may not have AI produce submitted work: P19, restrict because permission can lift it.
units.anchor: Don’t use GenAI to complete assignments unless you have explicit permission

units.why: Data falsification: "Don't use GenAI to generate or alter data in ways that misrepresent your findings". Ban on fabricating or falsifying data: P74.
units.anchor: Don’t use GenAI to generate or alter data in ways that misrepresent your findings

units.why: Collusion: "Don't share GenAI-generated work with others unless the instructor allows it." Closest is P127 (group work rules), but it is about sharing AI work; a partial fit.
units.anchor: Don’t share GenAI-generated work with others unless the instructor allows it
units.fit_note: A collusion rule about sharing AI-generated work, not rules for group projects.

units.why: Recommends a "university-wide system to evaluate and approve GenAI tools" for security, privacy and educational value: P65.
units.anchor: Establish an agile university-wide system to evaluate and approve GenAI tools

units.why: Recommends funding "institutional subscriptions to vetted GenAI tools" and infrastructure. An investment commitment, P122; equitable access is a stated aim.
units.anchor: Provide funding for institutional subscriptions to vetted GenAI tools
units.fit_note: Also ties subscriptions to equitable access (P51) and licensed tools (P92).

units.why: Recommends soliciting "input from faculty and staff" on resources to ease workload of integrating GenAI. Support for faculty: P63.
units.anchor: solicit input from faculty and staff to identify resources that can help alleviate the workload
units.fit_note: Support is framed as input-gathering on resources rather than training.

units.why: Recommends "GenAI literacy training programs for faculty, staff, and students": P70 (covers students, not faculty-only P63).
units.anchor: Implement GenAI literacy training programs for faculty, staff, and students

units.why: Recommends "a centralized hub or repository for GenAI-related resources" with approved tools and policy updates, directing readers to resources: P115.
units.anchor: Create a centralized hub or repository for GenAI-related resources
units.fit_note: A recommendation to build the hub, not a pointer to an existing one.

units.why: Recommends "targeted pilot programs to explore creative uses of GenAI". An institutional innovation commitment: P122; it gathers evidence (P55) only implicitly.
units.anchor: Initiate targeted pilot programs to explore creative uses of GenAI in teaching, learning, and assessment
units.fit_note: Pilots also "inform best practices" (P55).

units.why: The guidelines disclose that "GenAI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) were used to edit drafts". How the policy was made: P84, and it models disclosure.
units.anchor: GenAI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) were used to edit drafts for some of the sections
units.fit_note: Also an example of the institution disclosing its own AI use.

units.why: Describes the drafting process: "multiple committee meetings" and "small writing groups". P84 how the policy was made.
units.anchor: conceived through multiple committee meetings over the course of several months

units.why: Gives adoption and revision dates ("December 2, 2024", "March 7 and May 16, 2025"). P84 date and process of making the policy.
units.anchor: further revised for clarity and completeness on March 7 and May 16, 2025
units.fit_note: Revision history also evidences P54.

notes: Single university-layer document. No school or computing documents found by the collector; course layer deferred. One UNCOVERED unit: safe harbor for students who follow instructions when using a required tool.
